title: Veronese numerator compatibility with tensor-power transitions
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], L an invertible O_X-module [def-sc-invertible-module], d,n,b natural numbers, and s a degree-d element of the section ring of L [def-sc-invertible-section-ring]. For a section t of O_X tensor (L tensorPow d) tensorPow n, define a_n(t) as the underlying section-ring element of sectionRingVeroneseNumerator [def-sc-section-ring-veronese-fraction-map]. Then a_(n+b)(mulTensorPowSection(homOfGlobalSection(L tensorPow d,s_d),O_X,n,b)(t))=a_n(t)*s^b, with the transition from [def-sc-section-fraction-presentation]. No nonvanishing, reducedness, or regularity hypothesis is required.

source.place: Equation module-invert-s (Tag 0B5L), Lemma 01PW(2), and the Veronese localization in the proof of Lemma 01Q1

proof.text: Cover X by opens with a free generator of L. Induct on tensorPowAddIso and tensorPowMulIso to show that their maps preserve the corresponding tensor-power generators; the unitors remove the tensor-unit generator. The inverse numerator identification consequently preserves coefficient functions.

Locally write s=c times the degree-d generator and the numerator as f times its tensor-unit/tensor-power generator. homOfGlobalSection sends 1 to s and its b-th tensor power sends 1 to c^b times the degree-b*d generator. mulTensorPowSection and section-ring multiplication therefore both give coefficient f*c^b in degree (n+b)*d. Naturality identifies these calculations with restrictions; sheaf separatedness glues equality. This also proves the identity for d=0, n=0, b=0, or zero s, since no division occurs.

lean.statement:
theorem sectionRingVeroneseNumerator_transition
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (d : ℕ) (s : sectionRingGrade L d) (n b : ℕ)
    (t : Γ((𝟙_ X.Modules) ⊗ (L.tensorPow d).tensorPow n, ⊤)) :
    (sectionRingVeroneseNumerator X L d (n + b)
      ((mulTensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection (L.tensorPow d) (s.val d))
        (𝟙_ X.Modules) n b).app ⊤ t)).val =
      (sectionRingVeroneseNumerator X L d n t).val * s.val ^ b
